findings.evidence: In the diff, the section variables are `[CommRing R] [LinearOrder R] [NoZeroDivisors R] [CharZero R]` with no `IsStrictOrderedRing` or `Field`. The module docstring (lines 24-25) itself says agreement with evaluation holds 'over any ordered field'.
findings.fix: Describe only what the statement gives, e.g. 'the right-hand sign of `p'` equals the right-hand sign of `p - C (p.eval a)`'. Then add 'over an ordered field this is the sign of `p(x) - p(a)` just right of `a`; see `exists_sign_eval_derivative`'.
findings.issue: The `derivSignRight_derivative` docstring says the sign 'is positive exactly when `p` lies above `p(a)` immediately to the right of `a`'. That is a claim about evaluation, but the theorem lives in `section Derivative` under `[CommRing R] [LinearOrder R] [NoZeroDivisors R] [CharZero R]`. There the order need not respect the ring and the interval may be empty, as in ℤ. The theorem only equates two algebraic signs.

findings.evidence: Same `section Derivative` variables as above. The evaluation reading is only proved in `exists_sign_eval_derivative`, which is in `section OrderedField`.
findings.fix: Use the same fix: state the equality with `-(p - C (p.eval a)).derivSignLeft a`, and put the interval reading under an 'over an ordered field' clause that points to `exists_sign_eval_derivative`.
findings.issue: The `derivSignLeft_derivative` docstring has the same problem. It says the sign 'is positive exactly when `p` lies below `p(a)` immediately to the left of `a`', but the theorem is stated in the same ring-level section.

summary: The docstrings for `derivSignRight_derivative` and `derivSignLeft_derivative` describe evaluation behaviour next to `a`, which their ring-level setting does not support. The other new docstrings and the module-docstring paragraph are accurate.
